title: Catalog API Response and Pagination Alternatives
purpose: Describe the two competing Catalog API drafts and their required client behaviors without selecting an authoritative contract.

scope.text: The handoff covers draft A's GET /v1/items response as a JSON object with an items array and next_cursor string, draft A's next-page UI support, and draft B's GET /v1/items top-level JSON array with page and page_size query parameters.

requirements.text: GET /v1/items returns a JSON object with an items array and next_cursor string.
UI must support moving to the next page.
GET /v1/items returns a top-level JSON array
uses page and page_size query parameters

stories.text: If a human selects draft A, a catalog page can load the JSON object response and move to the next page.
acceptance_criteria: Given a human has selected draft A, when a catalog request is made, then the response is a JSON object containing an items array and a next_cursor string.
Given a human has selected draft A, when the user initiates moving to the next page, then the UI advances to the next page instead of remaining on the current page.

stories.text: If a human selects draft B, a catalog request returns a top-level JSON array and honors page and page_size query parameters.
acceptance_criteria: Given a human has selected draft B, when a catalog request is made, then the response is a top-level JSON array.
Given a human has selected draft B, when the request includes page and page_size query parameters, then the endpoint returns items according to those parameters.

edge_cases.text: The exact user action and visual change for moving to the next page are not specified in draft A.
The behavior for missing, invalid, or out-of-range page and page_size values is not specified in draft B.

dependencies.text: Neither draft is approved; the authoritative contract has not been selected.

risks.text: Selecting draft A would leave draft B's top-level JSON array and page/page_size contract unfulfilled; selecting draft B would leave draft A's JSON object with items array and next_cursor contract unfulfilled.

success_metrics.text: For whichever draft a human selects, a catalog request returns a response shape and pagination fields matching that selected draft.

open_questions: Which catalog API response shape and pagination mechanism should be treated as the authoritative contract: draft A (JSON object with items array and next_cursor), draft B (top-level JSON array with page and page_size), or a newly selected contract?
What exact user action triggers moving to the next page in draft A?
How should the API handle missing, invalid, or out-of-range page and page_size values in draft B?
Who has authority to select the authoritative contract?
